Which of the following statements are true concerning the function $y=f(x)$ whose graph is shown above? 

I. ${lim}_{x\to \,0}f(x)=3$

II. ${lim}_{x\to \,1}f(x)=3$

III. ${lim}_{x\to \,-1}f(x)={lim}_{x\to \,2}f(x)$
question.worked_solution:
Let's analyze each statement in turn.

- Statement I is false. As $x$ approaches $0$ from the left and right we get

$$
{lim}_{x\to \,{0}^{-}}f(x)=3,\,{lim}_{x\to \,{0}^{+}}f(x)=\text{DNE}\,.
$$

Therefore, ${lim}_{x\to \,0}f(x)=\text{DNE}.$

- Statement II is false. We see from the graph that 

$$
{lim}_{x\to \,{1}^{-}}f(x)=\text{DNE},\,{lim}_{x\to \,{1}^{+}}f(x)=3\,.
$$

Therefore, ${lim}_{x\to \,1}f(x)=\text{DNE}.$

- Statement III is true.  We see from the graph that 

$$
{lim}_{x\to \,-{1}^{-}}f(x)={lim}_{x\to \,-{1}^{+}}f(x)=2
$$

Hence, ${lim}_{x\to \,-1}f(x)=2.$ Meanwhile, 

$$
{lim}_{x\to \,{2}^{-}}f(x)={lim}_{x\to \,{2}^{+}}f(x)=2
$$

 
Hence ${lim}_{x\to \,2}f(x)=2.$ Therefore, ${lim}_{x\to \,0}f(x)={lim}_{x\to \,2}f(x).$

In conclusion, only statement III is true.
